key_insight: DLaR balances exploration and coherence in latent reasoning by adapting stochasticity at both individual reasoning steps and across training.
engineering_relevance: For LLM-based mathematical reasoning, DLaR offers a confidence-sensitive alternative to deterministic inference or uniform noise injection.
method: Use Adaptive Stochasticity Modulation to adjust latent-step perturbations via a confidence–entropy signal.
Use Training-Aware Stochasticity Tuning to progressively decay base stochasticity.
Combine both mechanisms within GRPO reinforcement learning.
evidence_signal: Across four in-distribution and three out-of-distribution math benchmarks, DLaR reports the highest average performance, with Pass@1/Pass@8 of 27.9%/50.6% on Llama-3.2-1B and 46.8%/68.2% on Qwen2.5-1.5B.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify training or inference overhead, leaving deployment cost and performance trade-offs unclear.
paper_title: DLaR: Dynamic Stochasticity Control for Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
